summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 3, part 4) describing a one-take film shoot inside an apartment. The narrator introduces the crew, including the cinematographer Roger Drexel, production manager Erica Cole, gaffer Ralph Cafiero, and sound recordist Tony Wills, all working for producer David Roth's Applecore Productions. The scene then shifts to the narrator arriving at Carly's apartment, where she is hesitant about the shoot but is persuaded to go ahead.
one_line: Excerpt from a novel in which a film crew sets up a one-take shoot in an apartment, and the narrator persuades the reluctant Carly to take part.
key_facts: The shoot was a one-take, all-or-nothing shoot, so the narrator sent down the full crew rather than only the key personnel.
Roger Drexel, a grizzled veteran with a ponytail, was the first cameraman and director of photography.
Roger Drexel had been with producer David Roth and his Applecore Productions since Drexel worked on beach movies and splatter films.
Erica Cole, described as the production manager, coordinated crew schedules and worked with Roger Drexel.
Greer Seiber, recently of NYU film school, handled the second camera.
Scott Ventri, another Applecore old-timer, was the key grip responsible for gear, setup, safety regulations and blacking out windows.
Ralph Cafiero was the chief electrician (gaffer) who temporarily hot-wired the apartment's circuit breaker to ensure enough amperage.
Paul Nulty, another NYU grad, worked on lighting as part of Ralph Cafiero's crew.
Tony Wills handled recording, and recorded the room's 'tone' the day before so it could be used in editing.
Sherry Moran, Tony Wills's girlfriend, served as mixer/recordist and assisted with the boom mike.
Arlene Morris, an old friend from the narrator's early days as an AD on the soaps, handled Carly's makeup and hair.
Carly, a successful publicity agent, is petite with dark hair and eyes and answered the door in pre-faded jeans and a striped sweater.
Carly said her nanny was there to keep her son Kevin out of the way.
Carly had cleared the living room, but she was biting her lip and said they should talk first.
The narrator settled on a sales point, asking 'Because you're totally crazy?', which made Carly laugh out loud.
